explanation: The execution contains a provenance fault introduced upstream. Job 1 correctly selected and retained all eight need records, but its provenance assembly emitted evidence_sources with record_id values set to the source ids (s01-s08) instead of the retained need record ids (n06-r01 through n06-r08). Job 2 then consumed that exact handoff, so its rank lookup by need record_id found no matches and every priority row has upstream_rank 0. The exact responsible function is supported by the visible source of assemble_provenance.
cited_evidence: The handoff evidence records exact hash handoffs for both needs and evidence_sources from job_upstream_demand_provenance to job_downstream_coverage_priority, so Job 2 consumed the upstream artifacts exactly.
Job 1 normalize output/needs_df retains 8 rows with the original need identity columns, matching the top-level corpus record ids n06-r01 through n06-r08.

Job 1 assemble_provenance source appends {'record_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_weight': ..., 'rank': index}, which replaces need record_id with source_id in the provenance table.
The downstream input evidence_sources contains record_id values s01 through s08, while downstream needs and coverage use record_id values n06-r01 through n06-r08.
Job 2 prioritize builds rank_by_record_id from evidence_sources record_id and looks up coverage.get('record_id'), producing observed priorities where every upstream_rank is 0.
